Hey, my classes on cellular metabolism are useful! Well lets talk about becoming ketone adapted!

First, lets start with how your body works. Your body is used to using carbs for energy, mainly. It can and does use proteins, nucleic acids, fatty acids if it wants to. It is also very capable of making any of these things into the others. Now when you starve (Im going to say starve but what I mean is "not having blood glucose above a certain level, because you are exercising/not eating"), your body uses up your glucose, then your starches and your fatty acids. Thats how you burn fat, you likely won't burn fat unless you get past your body using up favorable energy sources first.

Becoming ketone adapted, or keto-adapted is telling your body "carbs are not favourable" because you eat so little of them. Your body instead starts to use ketones instead of starches and stuff. Its less efficient. Thats why you lose weight. But its better for stamina, which is why some athletes do it.

But your body likes to use carbs, because its more efficient. If it CAN, it WILL. So if you keto-adapt yourself, you have to KEEP using proteins and fats for energy, you can't eat carbs at all or your body goes back. Is it a good idea? Maybe, if you are a stamina athlete. But stamina athletes generally exercise enough that weight control is not an issue. Can it be bad for you? Again...maybe. If you keep being keto-adapted for a long long time and weaken the processes for carbohydrate control, and then shock yourself by eating a whole cake or something, you might hurt yourself.

So in the end, it is a sham. Just eat less, its easier.
